I began by locating the ONS “Subnational gas consumption statistics” dataset, which contains domestic‑gas consumption figures for every local authority from 2005 – 2024. The dataset is hosted on the GOV.UK publishing service and is available both as an Excel file and as a single‑sheet CSV file (URL: <https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/69f9c094a40aa2232fede4af/gas_LA_stacked_2005-2024.csv>).

When I fetched the CSV, the tool returned only a short excerpt that included the 2005 values for the five unitary authorities in the question (Flintshire, County Durham, Bedford, North Lincolnshire and Telford & Wrekin). The excerpt did not contain any rows for 2012 or 2023, and the tool did not provide a way to retrieve the remainder of the file.

Because the 2012 and 2023 domestic‑gas consumption values (in GWh) for each of those authorities are not available in the data that I was able to download, I cannot calculate the change in consumption between 2012 and 2023, and therefore I cannot identify which authority had the largest drop.

I was unable to locate an alternative source or a more comprehensive download of the ONS dataset that includes the required years. If you have access to the full CSV/Excel file or another ONS resource that contains the 2012–2023 domestic‑gas consumption figures for these unitary authorities, please share it and I can proceed with the calculation.
